title: New LEGO Star Wars AT-AT lands with a launch-day discount
summary: The Mandalorian-era AT-AT walker is up for pre-order at Amazon UK with 8% off before it's even out the box, plus a price guarantee if it drops further.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A new four-legged friend is stomping onto shelves. LEGO Star Wars 75454 Imperial Remnant AT-AT with INT-4 is up for pre-order at Amazon UK, and someone's already knocked a chunk off the price before it's even launched. Get in.

Here's the damage:

- **Set:** 75454 Imperial Remnant AT-AT with INT-4
- **Price:** £128.99 at Amazon UK (down from RRP £139.99 – that's £11 off, 8%)
- **Pieces:** 1,453
- **Release date:** 1 August 2026
- **Minifigures:** seven in total – two brand new Imperial Remnant Snowtroopers, an Imperial Remnant Warlord, Din Djarin, Grogu, an AT-AT Driver and a regular Snowtrooper

This walker's a fresh take on the classic AT-AT, based on the version seen stomping through the opening of The Mandalorian and Grogu rather than the Hoth original. So even if you've already got a shelf groaning under the weight of an Empire Strikes Back AT-AT, this one's different enough to earn its spot.

Amazon's also chucking in a pre-order price guarantee, so if the price dips lower between now and launch day, you'll only pay the cheapest price going. Handy if you're the type who checks deal pages more often than the postman checks your street.

Eight percent isn't the biggest discount this set will ever see in its lifetime, but it beats the 5% cashback you'd get going through LEGO Insiders points – and this way the saving's real cash, not points locked in your account.

## Why it matters
Flagship LEGO Star Wars sets don't come cheap, and a decent day-one discount on a big vehicle set like this is rare. At £128.99 for 1,453 pieces and seven minifigures, it's already looking like better value than some of this year's other big Star Wars playsets.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on that price guarantee – if it drops further before 1 August, you'll want to make sure Amazon actually honours the lower price when it ships. Worth checking back closer to launch to see if other retailers match or beat the discount too.

title: LEGO Ideas Sea Serpent GWP vanishes in Australia in just 10 hours
summary: The free-with-purchase 40912 Sea Serpent sold out down under way ahead of schedule, so UK Castle fans might want to hurry before it slithers off shelves everywhere else too.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Castle fans, drop what you're doing. LEGO Ideas **40912 Sea Serpent** – a remake of the 1992 Black Knights classic 6057 Sea Serpent – has sold out in Australia and New Zealand roughly **10 hours** into what was meant to be a **six-day** gift-with-purchase window. Six days. Ten hours. This thing didn't sail off into the sunset, it launched itself off the shelf.

The GWP is tied to LEGO Insiders Days, which runs until **12 July**. Here's the deal, for now:

- **Set:** LEGO Ideas 40912 Sea Serpent
- **Free with orders over:** £160 (UK) / $180 (US) / €180 (Europe)
- **Qualifying discounted sets** during Insiders Days, plus double-points themes including Marvel, Harry Potter, Speed Champions, Jurassic World, Disney, Sonic the Hedgehog, Wicked and Education
- **Status:** SOLD OUT in Australia and New Zealand; still available in the UK, US and Europe at time of writing
- **Window:** originally running until 12 July, or while stocks last (looking increasingly like the latter)

If you miss out, don't panic entirely. Most of the build is doable with parts you've already got, Pick a Brick, or BrickLink. The only genuinely exclusive bits are **two new Black Knights shields** and the **fabric sail**. You'll survive without the shields. The sail's trickier – you'll either need to hunt one down separately or get creative with a brick-built alternative, because a Sea Serpent without a sail is just... a serpent.

## Why it matters
Beyond the BrickLink Designer Program, Castle fans have had precious little on shelves lately, so a proper nostalgic remake like this was always going to cause a stampede. Southern hemisphere stock shortages for GWPs aren't new for the LEGO Group, but a ten-hour sellout is a proper eyebrow-raiser and a pretty clear signal that demand massively outstripped supply everywhere it's launched so far.

## What to watch next
If Australia went in ten hours, the UK, US and European stock isn't guaranteed to make it to 12 July either. If you want this one on your shelf, treat it like the last brownie at a party – don't wait around admiring it.

title: Seven LEGO sets that nail the light brick trick
summary: Brick Fanatics has rounded up seven sets that use LEGO's humble light brick brilliantly, from X-ray hospitals to a glowing Eye of Sauron, ahead of the new E.T. set's August launch.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
That little 2x3 light brick has been quietly stealing the show in LEGO sets since it debuted back in 2006 with the BIONICLE and Creator Mythical Creatures themes. Brick Fanatics has picked out seven sets where it's used the piece to genuinely brilliant effect, and it's a proper trip down memory lane.

The list includes:

- **76467 Luna Lovegood's House** – £89.99 / $89.99 / €99.99, 764 pieces, released January 2026, available now. Light brick creates a shadow-puppet effect telling the Deathly Hallows story.
- **60204 City Hospital** – £69.99 / $99.99 / €79.99, 861 pieces, released June 2018, now retired. Lights up a hidden skeleton graphic to mimic an X-ray.
- **10273 Haunted House** – £209.99 / $249.99 / €229.99, 3,231 pieces, released May 2020, now retired. Light shines through a concealed layer behind a portrait for a spooky reveal.
- **21335 Motorised Lighthouse** – £259.99 / $299.99 / €299.99, 2,065 pieces, released September 2022, now retired. Pairs the light brick with a custom Fresnel lens and rotating mechanism for a real sweeping beam.
- **10333 The Lord of the Rings: Barad-dûr** – £399.99 / $459.99 / €459.99, 5,471 pieces, released June 2024, available now. The Eye of Sauron glows fiery orange atop the 83cm tower.
- **10275 Elf Club House** – £84.99 / $99.99 / €94.99, 1,197 pieces, released September 2021, now retired. A cosy glowing fireplace for festive display vibes.
- **21330 Home Alone** – £229.99 / $249.99 / €249.99, 3,955 pieces, released November 2021, available now. Recreates Kevin's terrifying furnace with an ominous glow.

The piece also flags 21370 E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, which launches 1 August and is up for pre-order now (£119.99 / $139.99 / €129.99), as a strong contender to join this list thanks to E.T.'s glowing finger.

## Why it matters
If you're after a display piece that does more than just sit there looking pretty, these sets show what the light brick can add to a shelf – atmosphere, storytelling, or just a proper wow moment when the lights go on. Handy shopping list too if you're hunting retired sets on the secondary market or deciding whether E.T. deserves a spot in your cart.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on reviews once 21370 E.T. lands in August to see if that glowing finger earns its place alongside the Eye of Sauron and the Haunted House in light brick hall-of-fame chat.

title: LEGO says F1 is now its 'number one priority' – and the pit lane's only getting busier
summary: LEGO's chief product officer has confirmed Formula 1 is one of the brand's most important themes right now, with more surprises promised for fans of Technic, Speed Champions and collectible helmets alike.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Since LEGO and Formula 1 officially teamed up back in 2024, the sets have been flying off shelves faster than a pit stop tyre change. Now Julia Goldin, LEGO's chief product and marketing officer, has told motorsport outlet The Race that F1 isn't just doing well — it's become one of the brand's biggest priorities full stop.

LEGO's actually been dabbling in F1-style builds since the mid-70s, with the odd Ferrari, McLaren or Williams tie-in over the decades. But it took until 2024 for a proper, fully branded range to land. Since then things have gone big: 1:1 scale LEGO cars before the 2025 Miami Grand Prix, LEGO trophies handed out at Silverstone, and a Minicar Drivers' Parade at last weekend's British GP.

According to Goldin, F1 ticks a rare box for LEGO — it's genuinely multi-generational and multi-gender. Women make up 42% of F1's global fanbase, with three in four new fans being women, so sets like:

- **43023 McLaren Mastercard F1 Team Lando Norris Helmet**
- **42240 Aston Martin Aramco AMR25 F1 Car**
- **11375 Ferrari F2004 & Michael Schumacher**

...are pulling in a broader crowd than your typical brick set. Goldin reckons F1 sets are even sitting in the top 10 with teen girls and women, which is not something you hear about most LEGO themes.

The range spans everything from collectible helmet builds like **43022 Scuderia Ferrari HP Lewis Hamilton Helmet**, to pocket-money-friendlier Speed Champions kit such as **77243 Oracle Red Bull Racing RB20 F1 Race Car**, right through to proper grown-up Technic engineering with **42171 Mercedes-AMG F1 W14 E Performance**. There's even LEGO City getting in on it with **60445 F1 Truck with RB20 & AMR24 F1 Cars**.

Goldin's take is that this spread — from simple builds to serious display pieces — is exactly the point. It lets kids get their heads round race principles while giving Technic fans an authentic engineering fix.

## Why it matters
If F1 really is LEGO's number one priority theme right now, expect the shelf space (and your wallet's workout) to keep growing. Whether you're into Speed Champions dashes, collectible helmets for the display cabinet, or full Technic builds, this is a theme LEGO clearly isn't slowing down on any time soon.

## What to watch next
Goldin confirmed F1 and F1 Academy remain LEGO's top focus going forward, hinting at more creative activations and surprises down the line — though no specific new sets or dates were mentioned yet. Watch this space.

title: Fan builder recreates Tokyo's lost Nakagin Capsule Tower in LEGO
summary: Builder Ids de Jong has turned the demolished Nakagin Capsule Tower into a glowing cyberpunk LEGO tribute, first shown at Skaerbaek Fan Weekend and now finally photographed in full.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fancy a bit of brick-built Tokyo on your shelf? Builder Ids de Jong has been dreaming about recreating the Nakagin Capsule Tower for ages, and now the finished MOC (My Own Creation, for the uninitiated) is out in the wild.

The real tower stood in central Tokyo until its demolition a few years back, and it's become a proper icon for architecture and sci-fi fans alike. Ids has leaned hard into that legacy, going for a lit-up, dystopian cyberpunk vibe rather than a straight museum replica.

A few standout details worth clocking:

- Full internal lighting for that broody, futuristic glow
- The distinctive stacked capsules that give the tower its name, rebuilt in miniature and clearly readable up close
- An angular, rust-coloured top section contrasted against yellowed whites lower down, nodding to the building's real-world weathering
- Brick-built Japanese signage worked into the design
- A cheeky nod to LEGO history, with printed elements borrowed from an early LEGO Star Wars set tucked into the build

The model actually debuted at Skaerbaek Fan Weekend last year, but it's taken this long for proper photos to surface. The Brothers Brick's own Jake snapped Ids stood proudly next to it at the show, so we finally get to see the thing in full glory.

## Why it matters
This isn't an official LEGO set, it's a fan-built custom model, but that's exactly why it's worth shouting about. It shows how far AFOL (Adult Fan of LEGO) builders push architecture and sci-fi themes using nothing but imagination, patience and a very good understanding of lighting. If you're into display builds, cyberpunk cityscapes, or just love seeing real buildings get a second life in plastic, this is the kind of thing worth bookmarking for inspiration.

## What to watch next
No word yet on whether Ids plans further Tokyo-inspired builds or if this one will do the rounds at other fan events. Worth keeping an eye on future convention appearances if you fancy seeing it in person.

title: Kaijune Roars In: LEGO Designers Unleash Their Inner Monster Builders
summary: It's Kaijune, the internet's monster-brick tradition, and a couple of actual LEGO set designers have popped up with their own kaiju MOCs. Teal, terrifying and made entirely of plastic.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
June's over but Kaijune's spirit lives on, apparently. You know the drill by now — brick builders spend a month channelling their inner monster movie fan, smashing together scaly, spiky, city-stomping creations for the fun of it. This year's crop is a bit thin on the ground compared to Aquajune's underwater takeover, but two names worth shouting about have joined in: actual LEGO set designers, moonlighting as AFOLs (that's Adult Fans Of LEGO, for the uninitiated).

- **Huib Versteeg**, LEGO Space legend turned pro designer, built **"Knife-Legs"** — a Pacific Rim-style kaiju rumoured (by the community, tongue firmly in cheek) to be Knifehead's smaller cousin. Teal has never looked so menacing.
- **Áron Gerencsér** (known online as Pohaturon) built **"Spikey Boy"**, putting the new Earth Elemental pieces from January's Ninjago wave to genuinely creative use. Small, cute, apparently very dangerous — we'll take their word for it.
- There's also a nod back to **Maxx Davidson's "kawaiiju"** creation from last year, too good not to mention twice.

No official LEGO Group involvement here — these are fan builds (MOCs, or "My Own Creations") shared by builders who happen to also design official sets for a living. No set numbers, no piece counts, no prices — just brick creativity doing its thing.

## Why it matters
It's a lovely reminder that the people designing your favourite official sets are still, underneath it all, the same brick nerds building silly monster mechs for fun in June. If you're hunting for MOC inspiration, or just fancy seeing what happens when Ninjago elemental pieces meet a Pacific Rim mood board, this is worth a scroll.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for whether a proper Kaiju LEGO Ideas set (Godzilla's been floated as a fan favourite) ever gets the official green light — that would be a very different kind of Kaijune altogether.

title: This LEGO Meduseld MOC is the Rohirrim upgrade your Middle-earth shelf needed
summary: Fan builder monsieur.kek has built a huge, gorgeous custom Golden Hall of Rohan, complete with SNOT wood-plank walls, a straw-tile roof and minifigs of Théoden and Éowyn.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
While we're all still admiring official LEGO Minas Tirith, one fan builder has quietly filled a gap the LEGO Group has left wide open since 2012.

MOC creator monsieur.kek has built a massive custom recreation of Meduseld, the Golden Hall of Rohan from Lord of the Rings, and it's a proper stunner. There's been no official Rohirrim set since Battle of Helm's Deep and the Uruk-Hai Army came out over a decade ago, so this build is doing some serious heavy lifting for Rohan fans.

Highlights from the build:
- SNOT (studs-not-on-top) pillars and upper walls that trick your eye into seeing real wooden planks
- Stacked cheese slopes above the golden arches for extra texture on the entrance
- A tan tiled roof echoing the Rivendell set's style, but recoloured to suggest straw thatching
- Side doors made from sideways plates and tiles, styled to look like they'd actually swing open
- A raised stone display platform with smooth tiling but enough exposed studs for minifigs
- Custom Théoden and Éowyn minifigs, with Théoden repurposing the new Unicorn Elf CMF hair piece to great effect

This is a fan-built creation, not an official LEGO product, so you won't find a set number or price tag here. It's built from standard LEGO elements though, which means techniques like these are fair game for your own MOCs.

## Why it matters
Rohan fans have been waiting a long, long time for their kingdom to get some love, and official sets haven't exactly rushed to fill the gap. Builds like this show what's possible with clever part choices and patience, and honestly this might be the closest thing to a proper LEGO Meduseld we'll see for a while. It's also a lovely companion piece if you've already got Minas Tirith taking pride of place on your shelf.

## What to watch next
No word on official LEGO Rohan sets, but Éowyn getting a fan minifig makes us wonder aloud whether LEGO might finally give her the official treatment. We'll keep our eyes peeled for more Middle-earth MOCs and any hints from LEGO's Lord of the Rings line.

title: BrickLink Designer Program swaps 'Series' for 'Waves' from 2028
summary: BrickLink has confirmed a shake-up to how it labels BDP releases from 2028, ditching 'Series' for 'Waves' and giving the packaging a fresh coat of paint.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
BrickLink has dropped official details on the next chapter of the BrickLink Designer Program (BDP), and it's mostly about names and looks rather than new sets themselves.

From the 2028 production year, BrickLink is retiring the word 'Series' in favour of 'Waves'. So what would've been Series 12 becomes **2028 Wave 1** instead. The idea is simple: the year's right there in the name, so you know roughly when your set's shipping without doing sums in your head.

Key bits confirmed by BrickLink:

- New naming kicks in from the **2028 production year** onwards
- Past releases keep their old names - Series 9, 10 and 11 aren't being renamed
- Maximum of **three Waves per year**
- Refreshed BDP icon - still bright orange, but a cleaner 1x1 tile design that scales better
- Boxes go largely blue (matching BrickLink's brand colour), with an accent colour per Wave: **Wave 1 = purple, Wave 2 = green, Wave 3 = red**
- BrickLink says there are **no further changes planned** beyond this naming and packaging refresh
- The programme itself isn't going anywhere - BrickLink confirmed it's continuing to grow

Worth remembering the BDP's history here too - it's been through a fair few makeovers already. Max quantities have crept from 5,000 up to 30,000+, and this is the third naming shift after Rounds became Series and now Series becomes Waves. Builders have also noted designers are now capped at one selection per year to spread the love around a bit more.

## Why it matters
If you're a regular BDP backer, this doesn't change what you can build - it changes how you'll find and track it. Clearer year-based naming should make it easier to spot when a set's actually landing on your doorstep, and the colour-coded packaging means less squinting at box art to work out which Wave you're holding. Handy for anyone building a collection and trying to keep their shelf (and their wallet) organised.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for the first 2028 submissions this Autumn - that's when we'll see the new Wave 1 branding and icon in the wild for real, rather than just in preview shots.

title: LEGO Insiders Days are here: free Sea Serpent, double points and juicy discounts
summary: LEGO.com's annual Insiders Days promos have kicked off, with a free Sea Serpent up for grabs and discounts on sets like the PAC-MAN Arcade — but you'll need to be quick, it all wraps up 12 July.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened

Right, wallets at the ready — LEGO Insiders Days have landed on LEGO.com and there's actually some decent stuff on offer this time.

Here's what's up for grabs:

- **40912 Sea Serpent** – free with any order over £160 / $180 / €180 (this is a proper GWP, not a discount)
- **5010033 Airplane – Special Edition** – free with any Creator, City or Friends purchase over £90 / $100 / €100
- **Double Insiders points** on Sonic the Hedgehog, Jurassic World, Speed Champions, Harry Potter, Marvel, Disney, Wicked and Education sets
- **Discounts** vary by region, but Europe's getting 20% off:
  - 10323 PAC-MAN Arcade
  - 10337 Lamborghini Countach 5000 Quattrovalvole
  - 21360 Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory

Worth noting — one Aussie fan's already reported the Sea Serpent sold out over there, so don't hang about if you fancy one. The whole promo runs until 12 July, or until stock runs dry, whichever comes first.

## Why it matters

Free sets and double points don't come round every week. If you were already planning a big LEGO.com order, timing it during this window could bag you an extra freebie or two without spending a penny more. Classic case of shop smart, not just shop fast.

## What to watch next

Keep an eye on stock levels for the Sea Serpent especially — GWPs have a nasty habit of vanishing before the official end date. Regional discounts may also shift, so it's worth checking your local LEGO.com store rather than assuming the UK gets identical pricing to Europe.

title: LEGO Pokémon just got its first ever minifigures, and there's a Poké Ball to hold them
summary: Five new LEGO Pokémon sets have been officially announced, headlined by a Poké Ball packed with the range's very first minifigures. Pre-orders are live now.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened

Right, put your Poké Balls away, LEGO's just released a real one. The LEGO Group and The Pokémon Company International have officially unveiled five new sets for the LEGO Pokémon range, and this time we're finally getting actual minifigures, not just those big brick-built creature displays.

The big one is the **Iconic Trainer Moments Poké Ball**, a brick-built Poké Ball that opens up to reveal scenes from a Trainer's journey, including a battle and Professor Oak's lab. Inside you get three minifigures (Professor Oak, Picnicker and Red) plus Pikachu and Eevee figures. That's the first proper minifigures this theme has ever had, so yes, it's a genuine moment.

Here's the full pre-order lineup:

- **72154 Iconic Trainer Moments Poké Ball** – 2,339 pieces – £229.99 / $299.99 / €249.99 – includes minifigures of Professor Oak, Picnicker and Red, plus Pikachu and Eevee figures
- **72150 Munchlax** – 757 pieces – £59.99 / $69.99 / €69.99 – poseable arms and head, over 18cm tall
- **72160 Arcanine** – 1,190 pieces – £89.99 / $99.99 / €99.99 – fully poseable display build
- **72168 Rayquaza** – 1,083 pieces – £119.99 / $119.99 / €129.99 – recreates the Sky Pillar scene from Omega Ruby/Alpha Sapphire, includes exclusive Lorekeeper Zinnia minifigure
- **40868 Up-Scaled Red Minifigure** – 930+ pieces – £69.99 / $79.99 / €79.99 – giant poseable Red figure with rotating head and Poké Ball

All five are up for pre-order now on LEGO.com. General release lands from 1st August 2026 via LEGO.com, LEGO Stores and selected retailers, though the big Poké Ball set (72154) holds back until 1st October 2026.

## Why it matters

LEGO Pokémon launched back in March with those large-scale creature builds, all lovely display pieces but no little figures to tell stories with. This is the first time the range has proper minifigures and character figures, which changes the game for anyone who wants to actually build scenes rather than just shelf ornaments. Throw in an exclusive Rayquaza minifigure and a Poké Ball you can genuinely open and close, and this feels like the theme growing up rather than just adding another creature to the collection.

## What to watch next

Worth keeping an eye on retailer stock once 1st August rolls around, big licensed launches like this tend to sell fast. And with minifigures now confirmed as part of the plan, don't be shocked if more Trainers and Pokémon pairs turn up down the line.
